newsitem.title: CHINA: HK STOCKS SEEN MAKING NEW HIGHS ON PROPERTY BUYING.
newsitem.headline: HK STOCKS SEEN MAKING NEW HIGHS ON PROPERTY BUYING.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to move further into record territory on Thursday, fueled by reawakened interest in property holding companies and positive sentiment generated by Wall Street, brokers said.
"We will be boosted slightly further because of better sentiment from the Dow overnight and interest in property and H shares," said Dennis Leung, research manager at J&A Securities (Hong Kong).
The Hang Seng Index soared to an all-time high of 16,600.59 on Wednesday, then eased to finish at a record high close of 16,541.60 on record high turnover of HK$31.85 billion.
Overnight, the Dow Industrials jumped 71.77 points, or 0.88 percent, to 8,259.31 after declining in three of its past four sessions.
The market is expected to continue to focus on the Cheung Kong group of companies rather than Swire, which is expected to report its earnings around noon (0400 GMT) on Thursday, brokers said.
Brokers said Cathay Pacific was expected to open lower after reporting a 35 percent fall in its first-half earnings on Wednesday.

"Until we see get a clearer picture of the Cheung Kong purchase of Jardine company shares, investors are going to hold these positions, and probably increase their weighting in Hutchison," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Hutchison hit an all time high of HK$82.75 on Wednesday, before easing to close up HK$2.50 at HK$81.25.
